question: A 52-year-old man with T2DM asks which staple he should prefer to reduce postprandial glucose excursions. Which recommendation is most consistent with ICMR-NIN 2020 dietary guidance for diabetes management?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: White polished rice has a high glycaemic index (~73) and causes rapid postprandial glucose spikes. It should be limited, not preferred, in T2DM dietary management.

Correct. Ragi (finger millet, GI ~69 but higher fibre, slower effective absorption) and other whole grains produce lower postprandial glucose excursions than refined cereals. ICMR-NIN 2020 recommends shifting toward whole grains, millets, and high-fibre foods in T2DM.
Maida (refined wheat flour) is high GI and lacks fibre; it causes rapid glucose absorption similar to white rice. Whole wheat atta is preferable to maida.
Even unsweetened fruit juice concentrates natural sugars without the fibre of whole fruit, causing a significant glycaemic response. Whole fruits (not juice) with lower GI are preferable in T2DM.

overallFeedback.feedback: ICMR-NIN 2020 recommends whole grains and millets over refined cereals in T2DM. Ragi and other millets provide fibre that slows glucose absorption, reducing postprandial spikes.
Correct! Millets (especially ragi) and whole grains are the ICMR-NIN 2020 recommended staple shift for T2DM — high fibre, sustained energy release, and lower postprandial glucose peaks.
